content: The Chelmsford Royal Commission, chaired by Justice John Patrick Slattery, was established by the New South Wales (NSW) state government between 1988 and 1990 to investigate mental health services in NSW. This commission was initiated following significant pressure from prominent Sydney radio and television programs, as well as advocacy efforts by the Citizens Commission on Human Rights, a group associated with the Church of Scientology. These entities urged the newly-elected Health Minister to fulfill his promises of establishing a Royal Commission. Initially, the commission's primary focus was intended to be on psychosurgery practices at the NSW Neuropsychiatric Institute. However, due to mounting media attention, the investigation shifted its focus to the controversial Deep Sleep Therapy conducted by Dr. Harry R. Bailey. Dr. Bailey served as the director of the Neuropsychiatric Institute from 1963 to 1979 and later directed the Chelmsford Private Hospital, a private psychiatric facility in Sydney. The public's growing concern and scrutiny led to the commission changing its title from Royal Commission into Mental Health Services to Royal Commission into Deep Sleep Therapy. Dr. Bailey, facing ongoing investigations into his medical practices, died by suicide in September 1985. In his suicide note, he wrote, Let it be known that the Scientologists and the forces of madness have won.
